llmResponse.agendaChanges: The board moved Section 6 (Strategic Resource Alignment presentation) before Section 5 (Public Comment) at the suggestion of Superintendent Baker and with board agreement; the Pledge of Allegiance (Section 2) was skipped for this meeting.

publicComments.name: Steven Jevic
publicComments.summary: Speaking on behalf of Orion PTO, he noted Orion's deep cuts last year, growing enrollment, and unique bilingual needs, and asked the board to take an equitable perspective before cutting the guest teacher position at Orion.

publicComments.name: Patricia Renderos
publicComments.summary: A Hoover parent speaking in Spanish, she asked the board to add a TK classroom, fund teachers so they don't leave, and provide coaching and professional development to retain teachers at Hoover.

publicComments.name: Agustín Espino
publicComments.summary: A Hoover parent asked the board to maintain mental health programs and TK, ensure the ratio of administrators and teachers has been adjusted for the smaller student population, and make equitable decisions for the Latino community.

publicComments.name: Lizbeth Estrada
publicComments.summary: A Hoover parent speaking in Spanish, she urged the board not to cut reading and math specialists or MTSS supports, warning that doing so would create long-term educational debt for struggling students.

publicComments.name: Christian Vasquez
publicComments.summary: A Clifford parent speaking in Spanish, he shared how the expanded resources available to his son compared to his older daughter's experience, and expressed concern about the impact of cutting specialists and support staff.

publicComments.name: Tina Yim
publicComments.summary: An Orion MI parent highlighted the growing fundraising burden on families due to district funding gaps and advocated for retaining Orion's bilingual guest teacher and continued district investment in the Mandarin Immersion program.

publicComments.name: Araceli Flores
publicComments.summary: A Hoover RLC teacher and alumna advocated for more resources, staffing, and support for special education students, stating that three full-time RLC teachers with minimal aide support are spread too thin.

publicComments.name: Lisa Onofre
publicComments.summary: A Clifford parent speaking in Spanish asked the board not to cut food services or cafeteria staff, to prioritize math education, and to refrain from selling district assets that should remain for school use.

publicComments.name: Tina Mercer
publicComments.summary: Roosevelt principal advocated for maintaining admin IEP sub coverage at TK-5 schools without assistant principals, noting her school alone has approximately 150 IEP meetings per year consuming roughly 250 hours of her time.

publicComments.name: Laura Ramirez
publicComments.summary: An Adelante Selby Spanish immersion parent asked the board to protect programs that directly impact student learning and wellbeing, including STEAM and arts, and to continue supporting family engagement organizations like Familias Unidas.

publicComments.name: Lilia Amalia Valdez
publicComments.summary: A Hoover parent shared how school counseling helped her son's anxiety after the pandemic and urged the board to protect counseling and mental health resources.

publicComments.name: Rita Melton
publicComments.summary: A 4th grade teacher at Adelante Selby advocated for preserving mental health professionals, MTSS TOSAs, and guest teachers, warning that cutting these positions increases burdens on principals and teachers and harms student achievement.

publicComments.name: Dora Ramirez
publicComments.summary: A Hoover parent with a child in special education asked the board not to cut music or STEAM, to provide extra math support, and to open more special education classrooms at the middle school level.
